description: I'm Nick, an inventor and AI systems builder entering the space mission design challenge with the Asteroid Belt Mining Continuum, a game about engineering drones for galactiforming. You design drones that fly, land, mine, replicate, and build waystations that support flight paths through the galaxy. We're seeking teammates into space science, mission design, engineering, coding, data analysis, or visual storytelling. Try it and reach out!
summary: Operation Cosmoform is a mobile-first 3D browser game where players engineer self-replicating drones that open the asteroid belt for human travel. Players design drone families (replicators, builders, miners, and payload transporters, with terraformer modules on every Nth drone) using Trajectory-Constrained Transform Algebra (TCTA), a design framework that takes each drone from its initial state to a design that meets the mission's goals and stays physically possible. Players then set the fleet ratio and launch the swarm. The drones fly to the best asteroid sites, land, turn into factory parts, mine, and build more drones. Haulers seed new factories, and the network builds waystations that turn asteroid ice into propellant and metals into parts ahead of the crewed ship.
details:
What it does and how it works
Operation Cosmoform is a mobile-first 3D browser game about building the infrastructure for human travel through the solar system. It opens with a short arcade sequence that plays mostly on its own and teaches the controls; a four-finger swipe skips it. Next, players design drones with Trajectory-Constrained Transform Algebra (TCTA), a framework created by Nicholas Hartman. TCTA takes each drone from its initial state to a final design, keeping every step within physical and mission constraints and reporting how much the design search was narrowed. Players build four drone families: replicators, builders, miners, and payload transporters. Each family has subtypes, and every Nth drone carries a terraformer module for growing food, lodging, and life support. Players then set the fleet ratio and launch.

In a real-scale 3D solar system, a swarm of about 100 drones flies to the best asteroid sites, lands, and transforms into factory components. The drones mine and build more drones. Haulers carry material to seed new factories, and the network builds waystations that turn asteroid ice into propellant and metals into parts, ready ahead of the crewed ship, the Marauder's Daughter. Players redirect drone groups with a tap, rally them with a hold, zoom with two fingers, and can ride along in first-person drone views. Six console panels share one mission state. The game also includes co-op for up to four roles, a competitive mode, scenarios, difficulty levels, a sandbox, saves, sharing, a leaderboard, and an optional post-game round where players plot Helium-3 mine sites along travel paths.

Benefits
The game teaches real mission-design trade-offs by letting players make them: delta-v and the rocket equation, Hohmann transfers, specific impulse for chemical and ion propulsion, solar power falling off with distance, Deep Space Network signal delay, and using resources found in space. It runs offline on any phone or tablet browser, with no install or login.

Intended impact
Sustained deep-space exploration depends on using resources that are already in space. We want students and the public to understand self-replicating infrastructure and asteroid resources as an engineering problem they can reason about, and to show that careful constraint-based design makes ambitious missions more achievable.

Tools, languages, hardware, and software
We wrote the game in HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with Three.js for 3D graphics and the Web Audio API for an original procedural soundtrack inspired by classic adventure games. Saves are stored in the browser with localStorage, and a Python script builds everything into a single self-contained file. We tested automatically with Playwright at phone and tablet screen sizes. The game is hosted on GitHub Pages. Asteroid data comes from the NASA JPL Small-Body Database, and players can import their own data in the same format. The demo video was made from real game footage with FFmpeg.

Creativity
Rather than flying one spacecraft, players design a self-building system, a von Neumann probe network. Its drones physically become the factories that make more drones. TCTA turns drone design into a visible step-by-step design path instead of a guessing game. The game ties the whole effort to one human story: making the way safe for the ship classically named : The Marauder's Daughter

Factors we considered

  • Scientific honesty: real JPL data is labeled as real, simulated values are labeled as simulated, future technology is marked as future technology, and TCTA is presented as a research framework, not a proven result.
  • A clear disclaimer that the game is not flight-certified.
  • Phone-first touch controls, no distortion on small screens, fast loading, and working offline.
  • Accessibility for beginners, with depth for experts.
  • Original music and art (HD-SI) human-directed-super intelligence used for music and graphics.
  • Realistic limits on power, distance, communication delay, and propellant.
